par2cmdline-turbo v1.4.0 (https://github.com/animetosho/par2cmdline-turbo, tag v1.4.0)
Vendored: src/, parpar/gf16/, parpar/hasher/, parpar/src/, COPYING.
CLI-only and OpenCL files are excluded from the build in Package.swift, not deleted.

LOCAL PATCHES (re-apply ALL of these when bumping the vendored version — every site is
marked with "MODERNPAR PATCH" in the source):

1. src/foreach_parallel.h — worker-thread exceptions are captured and rethrown on the
   calling thread instead of hitting std::terminate (bare std::thread path) or being
   silently swallowed (std::async wait() path); thread-creation failure mid-spawn joins
   already-started workers before rethrowing. Required for Par2Shim's cooperative
   cancellation, which throws from the output streambuf on engine threads.

2. parpar/gf16/threadqueue.h — MessageThread gains join() (wait for the thread to drain
   its queue and exit after end()).

3. parpar/gf16/controller_cpu.cpp — PAR2ProcCPU::_deinit() quiesces in dependency order
   (transferThread first — it submits compute work — then thWorkers) and JOINS everything
   before freeGf(). Resolves upstream's "TODO: join threads?". Without this, deinit during
   a cancellation unwind frees the GF context / staging buffers while kernels are still
   running them (use-after-free, SIGSEGV reproduced).

4. src/par2repairer.cpp + src/par2creator.cpp — destructors call parpar.deinit() BEFORE
   delete[] transferbuffer (workers read/write that buffer; with patch 3's joining deinit
   this ordering makes exception unwinds safe).

5. src/par2repairersourcefile.{h,cpp} + src/par2repairer.cpp — non-recovery source files
   (a FileDesc listed in the Main packet's NON-recovery set) are never passed to SetBlocks(),
   so their sourceblocks/targetblocks iterators stay default-constructed. Upstream dereferenced
   those unassigned iterators, SIGSEGV'ing on ANY non-recovery file with size > 0 — a crafted
   or third-party .par2 crashes the whole app because ModernPAR runs the verifier in-process.
   The fix adds a per-file flag Par2RepairerSourceFile::BlocksAllocated() (set true only in
   SetBlocks()) and gates every per-file block-iterator dereference on it, plus restricts the
   recovery accounting / repair machinery to RECOVERABLE files (index < RecoverableFileCount()):
     - VerifyDataFile whole-file "perfect match" loop: gate on the PER-FILE flag, not the
       repairer-global `blocksallocated` (which is true whenever ANY recoverable file was
       allocated). This is the originally-reported crash.
     - PrepareVerificationHashTable: only Load() a verification packet when the file's blocks
       were allocated, so a crafted IFSC packet attached to a non-recovery file can't make
       VerificationHashTable::Load walk its unassigned iterator.
     - UpdateVerificationResults: skip non-recovery files entirely (they have no recovery
       blocks and can't be repaired). This ALSO fixes a logic bug where an intact non-recovery
       file was counted into completefilecount, reaching RecoverableFileCount() and making
       Process() return eSuccess WITHOUT repairing a damaged recoverable file.
     - RenameTargetFiles / CreateTargetFiles: skip non-recovery files so the repair path never
       renames their on-disk copy aside or recreates a missing one (which walked TargetBlocks()).
   Regression test: Tests/ModernPARCoreTests/NonRecoveryCrashRegressionTests.swift (drives the
   in-process EmbeddedEngine against the crafted Fixtures/par2-nonrecovery/ set — reverting this
   patch turns the tests back into a SIGSEGV).

6. src/par2creator.cpp + src/par2creatorsourcefile.cpp + src/verificationpacket.cpp — empty
   (0-block) source files in CREATE. The CLI skips 0-byte files (commandline.cpp "Skipping 0
   byte file"), so upstream never exercises them, but libpar2's par2create() — which Par2Shim
   calls directly — accepts them. Upstream then wrote a 20-byte hash+CRC entry past the end
   of the empty file's 0-entry verification packet (heap overflow, ASan-reproduced) at two
   sites, and the first one also wrote wrong checksums. Upstream turbo HEAD, turbo v1.5.0 and Parchive
   par2cmdline HEAD all still have both.
     - ProcessData (single-pass with deferred hashing — the default path): the sourcefile
       iterator advanced only after ++sourceindex >= BlockCount(), so an empty file sorting
       (by FileId) before a non-empty one was handed the next real block. Every later block
       hash and full-file hash shifted by one block: the set reports intact data as damaged,
       and repairing it rewrites intact files with shifted content (the originals survive only
       as name.1). Fix: step over 0-block files when positioning the iterator, at loop entry
       and after each advance.
     - Par2CreatorSourceFile::Open (the non-deferred path: 0 recovery blocks, blocks over
       MAX_CHUNK_SIZE = 32 MiB — every automatic-size set over ~62.5 GiB — or recovery data
       beyond the memory limit): need starts at blocksize, so a "last block" was finalized for
       a file that has none. Fix: finalize only while blocknumber < blockcount.
   Guards added with it:
     - VerificationPacket::SetBlockHashAndCRC throws std::logic_error on an out-of-range block
       (its assert is compiled out by NDEBUG), so any future desync fails as
       PAR2SHIM_CXX_EXCEPTION instead of silently corrupting the heap.
     - ComputeBlockCount refuses a set with no source data (every file empty or unreadable —
       GetFileSize reports 0 for both). Upstream divided by the largest file's block count (0)
       when sizing scLimited volumes, then collided on output names; the other schemes wrote a
       useless 0-source-block set.
     - A source file that changes size during the create now fails it with eFileIOError. The
       size is read three times: ComputeBlockCount, Par2CreatorSourceFile::Open, and every
       (re)open in ProcessData (once per pass). CreateSourceBlocks refuses when the per-file
       block counts no longer add up — a grown file overflowed sourceblocks, and a shrunken one
       left blocks with no DiskFile (NULL dereference in ProcessData). ProcessData refuses when
       a file's size at (re)open differs from the size recorded at its first open — upstream
       hashed and encoded it truncated or zero-filled and "succeeded" with a set that cannot
       verify or repair. A change that keeps the size, or that happens after the engine's last
       read of the file, cannot be detected.
   Output for sets without empty files is byte-identical to upstream. The closing note below
   does not cover the refusals above: they replace upstream runs that "succeeded" by writing
   unusable sets. ModernPAR's create path
   still skips 0-byte files like the CLI (EmbeddedCreate.swift) — PAR2 readers, turbo and
   par2cmdline included, cannot tell two empty members of one set apart and report a false
   "wrong name" — so these patches keep the C ABI safe for any caller and cover a file that
   empties after that check. Regression tests: Tests/Par2KitTests/EmptyFileCreateTests.swift.

Success-path behavior is unchanged by all patches.

SHIM-SIDE MITIGATION (not a patch to this tree; re-check it on every bump):

- Par2Shim.cpp runs ONE engine operation per process at a time (a process-wide mutex around
  every repair/create). Upstream's first-use initializers — parpar/gf16/gfmat_coeff.c
  gfmat_init(), parpar/hasher/hasher.cpp setup_hasher(), parpar/gf16/gfmat_inv.cpp
  pmulInit/setup_pmul() — publish their "done" guard before the work is finished, and the
  Par2Repairer/Par2Creator filethreads statics are rewritten on every run. Operations racing
  through first use see NULL or half-built GF(2^16) tables (a crash, or wrong recovery data
  from a create); in unoptimized builds gfmat_init()'s in-place reciprocal pass leaves the
  table corrupt for the life of the process, so every later repair failed verification
  (reproduced with concurrent creates). Only relax the lock if upstream makes all of these
  thread-safe.
